# Redundant Coding

## Redundant coding

- Color alone can fail: many categories, tiny elements, or cvd
- **Redundant coding:** encode the same information in more than one way
- Shape, line type, position, direct labels, legend order
- Always makes it easier to read the figure, and often removes the legend

## Color alone: iris species

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Three groups, yet hard to read
- Green *virginica* and blue *versicolor* are hard to tell apart
- Points are otherwise identical

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-iris-one-shape", fig_iris_one_shape(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Color alone under cvd

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Deuteranomaly and protanomaly: green and blue look more distinct
- Tritanomaly: blue and green look similar
- Grayscale: no species can be told apart

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-iris-one-shape-cvd", fig_iris_one_shape_cvd(),
          w = 6, h = 4.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Add shapes, swap colors

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Swap the colors for *setosa* and *versicolor* so blue is no longer next to green
- Give each species its own point shape
- Both fixes are cheap

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-iris-three-shapes", fig_iris_three_shapes(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Legible under cvd and in grayscale

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- With shapes, even the fully desaturated version works
- Dashed lines for line plots are usually a poor substitute: visual noise, hard to match to the legend

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-iris-three-shapes-cvd", fig_iris_three_shapes_cvd(),
          w = 6, h = 4.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Legend order matters

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Four stocks, indexed to 100 in June 2012
- Lines have a clear visual order: Facebook on top, Apple at the bottom
- The legend is alphabetical, so the reader has to work to match them

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-tech-stocks-bad-legend", fig_tech_stocks_bad_legend(),
          w = 5, h = 3.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Match legend order to the data

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Reorder the legend to match the perceived order of the lines
- Autogenerated legends sort alphabetically, with no knowledge of the picture

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-tech-stocks-good-legend", fig_tech_stocks_good_legend(),
          w = 5, h = 3.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## The benefit shows under cvd

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- In tritanomaly and grayscale, blue and green are close, but the order still tells us which line is which
- Microsoft and Apple are darker and take the bottom two spots

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-tech-stocks-good-legend-cvd", fig_tech_stocks_good_legend_cvd(),
          w = 6, h = 4.4, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Better still: no legend

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A legend forces the reader to move information from one part of the figure to another
- **Direct labeling:** put names next to the data
- Do not just describe colors in the caption

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-tech-stocks-no-legend", fig_tech_stocks_no_legend(),
          w = 5.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Direct labeling for groups

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- For scatter plots, label groups, not points
- Draw ellipses around the majority of the points and label them
- Color the label like the data, but darker, so it stays legible

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-iris-ellipses", fig_iris_ellipses(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## Direct labeling for densities

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Label each curve with its species name
- Thin colored text looks lighter than a filled area of the same color: darken it
- Marginal densities around a scatter plot can also replace the legend

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
:::
::::

```{r}
#| output: asis
place_fig("fig-iris-densities", fig_iris_densities(),
          w = 4.5, h = 3.6, x = 8, y = 2, width = 7.5)
```

## One variable, one legend

- When one variable maps to several aesthetics (position and color), use one legend-like element
- Integrate the color bar into the axis it duplicates
- Example: temperature on the x axis and as color, with the color bar along the axis
